role: The append-only record of every time bytes from a private staging area became authoritative bytes in the canonical estate. Private staging has NO authority until it is promoted, and a promotion is an event with digests and an accountable reviewer — never a copy command.
why: This estate is gitignored. It has no diff of its own, so the only trace of staged bytes replacing authoritative bytes was that the authoritative bytes changed — and nothing anywhere could tell that from the estate having always said so. Four of five estate copies on this host were, until today, indistinguishable from the canonical estate, and one of them declared its private staging INSIDE the canonical estate root. Either could have written through with no event.

rules.append_only: Entries are appended and never rewritten or reordered. `sequence` is dense and starts at 1; a gap is a removed event and a repeat is a rewritten one, and tools/check-canonical-estate.mjs rejects both.
rules.digest_bound: Every event carries source_sha256 (what came in) and resulting_sha256 (what the canonical path became). The resulting body is retained content-addressed under _archive/evidence/cas/ before the event is appended, so a promotion can always be reproduced and disputed.
rules.post_promotion_drift_is_reported: On every run the checker re-digests each promoted target. If the bytes no longer match the last promotion for that path and no later promotion supersedes it, that is an unrecorded mutation of authoritative bytes and is reported as one.
rules.staging_is_outside: A private staging directory lives OUTSIDE the canonical estate tree. Staging held inside the estate is one boundary-file edit away from being scanned as authoritative, and that edit would not look like a promotion.
rules.accountable: reviewer_ref and reason are mandatory. An unattributed promotion is a file copy wearing a ledger entry.

claim_boundary: A promotion event records that specific bytes entered the canonical estate under a named reviewer at a named time. It asserts nothing about whether those bytes are correct, sufficient, or reviewed on their merits, closes nothing, and grants no coverage.
